<issue>
LB listener port for cilium-etcd's etcd cluster not created on GCE
/kind bug

**1. What `kops` version are you running? The command `kops version`, will display
 this information.**

Client version: 1.33.1 (git-v1.33.1)

**2. What Kubernetes version are you running? `kubectl version` will print the
 version if a cluster is running or provide the Kubernetes version specified as
 a `kops` flag.**

**3. What cloud provider are you using?**

GCE

**4. What commands did you run?  What is the simplest way to reproduce this issue?**

kops create cluster cluster.k8s.local \
  --topology private \
  --api-loadbalancer-type internal \
  --networking cilium-etcd \
  --bastion

**5. What happened after the commands executed?**

Cluster built, but cilium pod continually restarted as they couldn't reach APISERVER:4003.  Confirmed that APISERVER isn't configured to listen on port 4003.

**6. What did you expect to happen?**

content.text:
I added the missing listener for cilium-etcd on GCE, but I haven't built it or run any tests. I also haven't checked that nodes can reach port 4003 through the firewall.

**Change:** in `createInternalLB` (`pkg/model/gcemodel/api_loadbalancer.go`), when Cilium has `EtcdManaged` set, each subnet now gets an extra internal forwarding rule. It is named `etcd-cilium-<subnet>` and sends TCP 4003 (`EtcdCiliumClientPort`) to the same backend service as the API rule. The shared IP address is also tagged with the `EtcdCilium` well-known service. The condition is the same one the AWS model uses for its etcd-cilium listener.

**Scope:** this only covers the internal load balancer, which is what the reproduction command (`--api-loadbalancer-type internal`) uses. A public GCE load balancer would not get a 4003 rule from this change.

**Firewall:** I didn't add a firewall rule for 4003. Traffic from nodes inside the network may already be allowed by existing rules, but I didn't confirm that.

**Tests:** existing GCE model tests with expected output may need updating if any use `cilium-etcd`. I haven't looked.
